capabilities: Generate a table of contents in a folder note via a trigger comment (%% Waypoint %%)
Update waypoints automatically when files or folders are created, renamed, moved, or deleted
Make folders appear in the graph view by linking their contents
Control category depth with nested waypoints and intermediary landmarks
extras: Development is in maintenance mode with no new features planned; the author points users wanting more QOL features to Obsidian Folder Overview. Waypoints are written as plain markdown links, so they remain usable outside Obsidian, but moving files in another editor leaves them stale.
intentEvidence: Waypoint was created to give users fine-grained control over what folders are significant enough to be considered
motivation: The author found tags inconvenient because they must be maintained manually and cannot nest meaningfully, while folders already encode category relationships.
problem: Folders are invisible in the graph view and keeping tags or index links current requires manual bookkeeping whenever files are created, renamed, or moved.

relations.evidence: Zoottelkeeper and other related plugins are more complex and try to solve different problems.
it is highly recommended that you install a plugin like Folder Note
For a clean alternative that is slightly less portable but has many QOL features

summary: Folder-note plugin that auto-generates tables of contents (MOCs) inside folder notes, linking every note in the folder and subfolders.
